W5 (contrarian), after E035. The tip is E035: E034's recipe plus prepare-side systems work. It runs 5.446 s and scores 0.7548 on seeds 0–2. Its held-out seeds 3–12 mean has not been measured; E034 passed the ≥0.7545 gate.

1. "Math-identical" is not bit-identical (my new mechanism, from my E035 miss). E035 shifted the per-seed results: 0.7539 → 0.7548. Possible causes:
- the order of the fp16 casts in prepare;
- the full synthetic trial now run in build, which changes cuDNN-benchmark and inductor algorithm choices, or allocator layouts that affect which algorithms get picked.

In this loop, code identity gives determinism (E003 and E004 matched exactly), but any change to the build or warm-up path can re-roll the numerics. So any edit, including a systems one, is a new 3-seed draw with SD about 0.15 pp. E035's +0.09 pp is noise, and the tip's 0.7548 probably carries about +0.05 pp of luck. Keep decisions on systems edits should be judged on time alone.

2. Settled by reading the code:
- Muon has no wd and renormalizes the filters every step (H1.5.4 is settled). Newton-Schulz already runs 3 steps.
- The whitening bias lr goes to 0 at 75 of 232 steps (about 32%), but its backward runs until the freeze at 75%.
- MaxPool comes before BN in every group, so group-1 BN runs on 15×15 maps. Only conv1's output and the pool see 31×31 traffic.

3. Where the stem's cost sits. E028 saved about 15 ms per truncated 32 px step, but inside E034 the realized saving was only about 0.65 s (net of the +0.5 epoch). Model it as about 12 ms per 32 px step and about 9 ms per 28 px step. The cost is conv1's 31×31×128 output, the pool backward, and conv1's wgrad and dgrad. The following pay little, about 1–2% each:
- whitening-only detach (I054): conv1's dgrad into a 24-channel input is small;
- BN folding (I057): the BN is at 15×15.

4. Prepare overhead is nearly exhausted. E035 cut about 0.035 s, so H3.2 and H3.2.1 fall short of their 0.05 s bar.

5. Resolution. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 28/32 px tail and the jump into 32 px carry the accuracy (E011, E018, E024).

6. Dials:
- Epochs: about 0.25 epoch ≈ 0.13 s ≈ 0.12 pp.
- Freeze dose from 75% to 60%: about 0.35 s for about 0.2–0.35 pp, because group 1 never adapts to 32 px. This roughly matches the epoch dial, so I expect it to be marginal.

7. Muon on CIFAR-100 is worth about 0.4–0.8 pp. Dropping it saves only about 2–3% of time.

8. Noise and fixes:
- Time-neutral "boosters" have mostly lost (E025, E029, E030, E032). The airbench defaults are near a local optimum, and every change pays a re-roll.
- 3-seed SD is about 0.15 pp; the 10-seed held-out SE is about 0.08 pp.
- Winner's curse on seeds 3–12 is about 0.05–0.1 pp. I expect fresh seeds 13–22 to land at about 0.7535–0.754, still above the 40-seed bar of 0.75 by about 0.3 pp.

Unsure:
- The compute vs bandwidth split (I058).
- How bandwidth-bound levers transfer to the PCIe judge.
- Whether the tip's held-out mean dropped after E035's re-roll.

forecasts.reason: The whitening bias already stops at about 32% (not before 25%), so the run goes ahead. But conv1's dgrad into a 24-channel input is small, so the saving should be about 1–2.5%, near the 2% bar, plus a re-roll.

There are about 35 more truncated steps at 9–12 ms each, so the time cut is real. But group 1 freezes before ever seeing 32 px, so I expect a held-out loss of about 0.2–0.3 pp, above the 0.15 pp allowed.
Winner's curse is about 0.05–0.1 pp, so fresh seeds should land at about 0.7535, within 0.15 pp of the held-out mean, with a pooled mean of about 0.754 (≥0.753).
Group-1 BN sits after the pool on 15×15 maps and runs forward-only once frozen, so folding it saves about 1%, short of the 2% bar, and the change re-rolls the seeds.
Diagnostic. I expect non-GEMM kernels to take at least 30% of the fp16 step, and conv1's 31×31 output plus its pool and backward to put group 1 and whitening at about 35–40% of the step.
Muon's gain on CIFAR-100 short runs is probably 0.4–0.8 pp, while Newton-Schulz costs only about 2–3% of time.

cruxes: Why did E035, meant to be math-identical, change the per-seed accuracies? Was it the cast order in prepare, or algorithm and allocator reselection after the synthetic trial added to build? If build-path edits re-roll the numerics, every systems lever is also a seed re-draw and should be judged on time only.

What does the tip (E035) score on held-out and fresh seeds? If its population mean is about 0.7535 rather than 0.7545, there is no margin left to spend on the freeze-dose or I054 trims without an epoch top-up.

Per-step profiler split: how much of the remaining stem cost is conv1's 31×31 output and backward, and how much is host and optimizer overhead? This sets whether any stem lever beyond the freeze dose is worth more than 2%.
